feature: See the number you are parking
summary: Placing a distance measurement now shows the actual number under your pointer while you aim the third click, instead of only a thin bracket, so where the number will sit is something you aim at rather than find out after you commit.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Open any screenshot. No flags to turn on.

try.do: Press I to pick the measure tool, and set the mode to Distance.
Click the left edge of a button, then its right edge.
Move the pointer down into the space under the button, and stop there.
Look at the number riding under the pointer: that is the pill, at its real size, with the real measurement in it.
Move up and down a little and watch it follow.
Check that it landed exactly where the preview had it.
Try it again with the third click above the button, and with a vertical measurement.

evaluate: Does the number following your pointer help you choose a spot, or does it get in the way of seeing what you are measuring?
Did the number land exactly where the preview showed it, every time?
The dot that used to mark the head is gone, since the number sits there now. Do you miss it?
At a zoomed-in canvas, does the previewed number look as crisp as the one that lands?
Is the preview quick enough that it feels attached to the pointer?
rough: This does not change where the number goes, only what you can see while choosing. The number still centres on your click, so parking it in a gap narrower than the number is tall still leaves it touching the thing you measured. That is now a decision card: 'When you click to park a distance number, which part of the number should land on your click?'
The preview shows up for Distance only. Size and Gap already draw their whole caliper, number included, on hover, so they never needed it.
